obligations.proposition: A stale price quote cannot authorize a settlement.
The same logical settlement cannot settle twice.
A settlement requires explicit authorization and matching scope.
Recognition of a foreign instrument preserves origin and does not mint local issuance.
Correction preserves the historical economic event lineage.
A dispute cannot be silently promoted to settled state.
A production observation does not itself create economic entitlement.
Labor observation does not itself determine compensation.
Unit identity and validity must match before cross-system valuation is applied.
Economic-event evidence provenance survives adapter translation.
A transport acknowledgment is not a settlement receipt.
Price and valuation basis remain distinct semantic objects.
An Integral CDS recommendation cannot itself become a decision or authorization.
An Integral OAD certification cannot itself become a production observation.
An Integral COS labor observation cannot itself mint an ITC entitlement.
An ITC entitlement remains instrument-specific and cannot silently become a generic Mycelix currency.
An Integral FRS recommendation cannot itself authorize an economic settlement.
An Integral source identity and policy version survive economic adapter translation.
A foreign Integral instrument may be recognized without creating local issuance.
Integral economic meaning remains reversible to its source observation, decision, or entitlement.
Settlement eligibility is distinct from authorization and requires current evidence, versioned policy, explicit authority, resolved disputes, and preserved claim ceiling.
An authorized submission cannot bypass explicit settlement eligibility.
An unresolved dispute cannot silently become settlement eligibility.
An indeterminate outcome cannot be treated as settlement success.
A settlement retry changes attempt identity but not logical economic identity.
Economic profile selection cannot silently change the source claim ceiling.
An external instrument profile cannot be admitted without the identity fields required by its profile class.
Issuer, network, chain, contract or mint identity cannot be silently dropped when required by the source profile.
A numeric quantity cannot change semantic unit or atomic scale during adapter translation without explicit policy and evidence.
A token ticker or display symbol cannot substitute for authoritative instrument identity.
A chain observation cannot itself establish legal ownership or key control.
A wrapped or bridged representation cannot silently become the underlying native asset.
A stablecoin representation cannot silently become the referenced fiat unit.
An FX conversion requires an explicit, versioned and validity-bounded valuation profile.
External provider status or transport completion cannot itself establish settlement finality.
External instrument recognition creates a distinct target identity and preserves source origin.
A profile adapter may restrict kernel transitions but cannot widen the source claim ceiling.
A simulation-scoped economic asset cannot silently promote its claim ceiling to a physical-world economic fact.
Settlement rail identity remains distinct from instrument identity.
Confirmation state cannot be interpreted as universal finality.
Provider acknowledgement cannot itself establish rail finality.
Block inclusion cannot itself establish economic settlement finality.
Probabilistic and consensus-finality profiles remain semantically distinct.
A settlement receipt cannot exceed its authorization scope.
Reconciliation requires explicit correspondence between source event, rail execution and target settlement identity.
Reconciliation mismatch cannot be promoted to successful settlement.
Timeout or unresolved rail outcome remains indeterminate until fresh qualified evidence resolves it.
A correction appends settlement-receipt lineage and does not mutate the original receipt.
Accounting projections cannot establish settlement finality.
A rail profile cannot widen the instrument profile claim ceiling.

claim_ceiling: Semantic economic interoperability only; no financial, legal, regulatory, or real-world performance claim.
